EMS GENERATED ALARM|HVAC - COMP OFF, HIGH PRESSURE-1

STORE COMPLAINT: Blowing hot air no thermostat in store. - REMOTE FINDINGS: RTU2 Y1 is being impacted by high suction line pressure (Y1 LOW: 176.6 PSI), negatively impacting the unit's cooling performance. Furthermore, RTU2's Zone Temperature sensor is offline (flatlined at 45ºF), leaving the Return Air Temperature sensor to determine Cooling/Heating needs as a backup. Additionally, RTU1 and RTU2 VFDs have been bypassed and are not communicating, preventing verification of active alarms or faults. Please inspect both units for any mechanical and/or electrical deficiencies, restore EMS control to the VFDs, and ensure they are set to AUTO mode. RTU3 (DOAS) no remote issues were found. - TECHNICIANS: If further assistance is required, you may contact Tutenlabs (855-298-7617) to verify unit operation once work is complete.

custom_fields.name: Client Quote
custom_fields.value:
Tech Reported that the Taylor margarita machine is leaking from the drive shaft assembly due to worn seals and bearing components

Note to Customer:
Any additional damage unrelated to the leaking drive shaft assembly discovered during disassembly, including damage to the freezing cylinder, gearbox, refrigeration components, or electrical controls, is outside the current scope of work and will require a separate quotation and prior approval before repairs are performed.

Required is to
Perform full inspection of the work area
Disconnect electrical power and secure the machine for service
Drain and remove all product from the affected freezing cylinder
Disassemble the drive shaft assembly and rear bearing housing
Remove and dispose of the existing beater drive shaft
Remove and dispose of the existing rear bearing assembly
Remove and dispose of all drive shaft seals, O-rings, and wear components
Inspect the drive coupling for wear or damage
Supply and install a new OEM beater drive shaft
Supply and install a new OEM rear bearing assembly
Supply and install new OEM drive shaft seals and O-rings
Supply and install a new OEM drive coupling if wear is found during disassembly
Lubricate all required components with NSF-approved food-grade lubricant
Reassemble the freezing cylinder and drive assembly in accordance with Taylor manufacturer specifications
Refill the machine with product and purge all air from the freezing cylinder
Test the machine through multiple freeze and dispense cycles
Verify proper beater operation, freezing performance, and confirm the leak has been eliminated
Final testing and commissioning
Clean the work area

Tech Reported that the roof vent opening has separated at the curb transition, creating an open gap that is allowing water intrusion and has damaged approximately 145 square feet of the interior drywall ceiling

Required is to
Perform full inspection of the work area
Protect adjacent roofing surfaces and interior finishes
Remove existing failed sealants, flashing materials and temporary repairs surrounding the vent curb opening
Remove deteriorated waterproofing materials from the vent transition
Realign and secure the vent curb and sheet metal transition
Repair the separated vent opening and eliminate all gaps between the duct transition and roof curb
Fabricate and install new galvanized sheet metal closure pieces to restore a continuous weather-tight transition
Install new flashing and reinforced roofing membrane around the vent curb assembly
Seal all joints, seams, corners, fasteners and transition points with compatible commercial-grade roofing sealant
Perform a controlled water test to verify the vent penetration is completely watertight
Remove and dispose of approximately 145 square feet of water-damaged drywall ceiling
Inspect the ceiling cavity, framing and insulation for moisture damage
Supply and install new drywall to match the existing ceiling
Tape, float and sand all drywall joints to a smooth finish
Apply stain-blocking primer to repaired surfaces
Apply two coats of matching ceiling paint to the repaired ceiling area
Verify the repaired vent opening is free of water intrusion
Perform final testing and commissioning
Clean the work area

Tech Reported that all three rooftop HVAC units require comprehensive troubleshooting and refrigerant leak testing to identify deficiencies affecting system performance

Required is to
Perform full inspection of the work area
Isolate electrical power to all three rooftop HVAC units
Perform comprehensive troubleshooting of the electrical, control and refrigeration systems
Inspect thermostats, control boards, transformers, contactors, capacitors, compressors, blower motors, condenser fan motors, evaporator coils, condenser coils, condensate drain systems and electrical connections
Connect digital refrigeration gauges and record operating pressures for all refrigeration circuits
Perform electronic refrigerant leak detection on all three units
Perform nitrogen pressure leak testing on all refrigeration circuits
Leak test evaporator coils, condenser coils, refrigerant piping, service valves, Schrader cores and all brazed joints
Restore power and verify unit operation
Perform final testing and commissioning
Clean the work area

Incurred:
Trip  $75.00

Leak test   $50.00

Tax 8.25% $58.20

Additional Repair:

Tech Reported that RTU #1 has reduced cooling efficiency due to a deteriorated condenser coil and lack of preventive maintenance, RTU #2 has a leaking evaporator coil resulting in low refrigerant pressure and loss of cooling capacity, and RTU #3 requires preventive maintenance due to heavy coil contamination and restricted airflow

Required is to
Isolate electrical power to all three rooftop HVAC units

RTU #1:
Remove and dispose of existing air filters
Supply and install new OEM air filters
Perform chemical cleaning of the condenser coil
Clean the evaporator coil, blower section and return air compartment
Flush condensate drain line and prime condensate trap
Inspect condenser fan motors, blower motors, capacitors, contactors and electrical connections
Restore power and verify refrigerant pressures, airflow, temperature split and overall cooling performance
If condenser coil efficiency cannot be restored following cleaning, replacement of the condenser coil will be required under a separate proposal

RTU #2:
Recover refrigerant from the refrigeration circuit in accordance with EPA regulations
Remove and dispose of the failed evaporator coil assembly
Supply and install new OEM evaporator coil assembly
Remove and dispose of the existing liquid line filter drier
Supply and install new liquid line filter drier
Braze refrigerant piping using nitrogen purge
Pressure test refrigerant circuit with nitrogen
Perform deep vacuum to remove moisture and non-condensable
Recharge system with the manufacturer-specified type and quantity of refrigerant
Replace pipe insulation removed during repairs
Restore electrical power
Verify refrigerant pressures, superheat, subcooling, compressor amperage, airflow and temperature split
Confirm proper cooling performance

RTU #3:
Remove and dispose of existing air filters
Supply and install new OEM air filters
Perform chemical cleaning of the condenser coil
Perform chemical cleaning of the evaporator coil
Clean blower compartment, return air section and condensate drain pan
Flush condensate drain line and prime condensate trap
Inspect blower motors, condenser fan motors, belts, capacitors, contactors and electrical connections
Restore power and verify refrigerant pressures, airflow, temperature split and overall cooling performance

All Three Units;
Verify thermostat operation and communication
Test each unit through complete cooling cycles
Confirm all systems are operating within manufacturer specifications
Perform final testing and commissioning
Clean the work area

Tech Reported that the restroom sheet linoleum flooring has deteriorated, the toilet flange has failed, and the subfloor has sustained water damage requiring repair and restoration

Required is to
Perform full inspection of the work area
Shut off the water supply to the toilet
Remove the toilet and dispose of the existing wax ring and toilet flange
Remove and dispose of all deteriorated sheet linoleum flooring and existing adhesive within the affected area
Remove all remaining adhesive and loose flooring materials
Remove and replace damaged subfloor sections
Reinforce and level the repaired subfloor to provide a stable installation surface
Supply and install new toilet flange securely fastened to the finished floor
Supply and install commercial sheet linoleum flooring to match the existing color and finish
Heat weld or chemically seal seams where applicable
Roll flooring to ensure proper adhesive bond and eliminate air pockets
Allow flooring adhesive to cure in accordance with manufacturer specifications
Supply and install new wax ring 
Reinstall and secure the existing toilet
Restore the water supply and verify proper toilet operation
Test for leaks at the flange, wax ring, and water supply connections
Verify the floor is level, secure and free of movement
Perform final testing and commissioning
Clean the work area

Note to Customer:
Any concealed water damage, deteriorated framing, mold, or additional substrate deterioration discovered after demolition is outside the current scope and may require a supplemental quotation.

Tech reported that the garage door and the metal sheet the side of the building are damaged

Required is to
Perform full assessment of the garage door opening and surrounding structure
Secure the work area and ensure the opening is safe from further collapse or hazards
Supply exterior-grade plywood sized to fully cover the opening
Construct a temporary wooden framing system
Supply and install wood studs and blocking to reinforce the plywood door assembly
Secure the plywood panels to the framing using fasteners
Ensure the temporary plywood door is properly aligned and tightly sealed
Reinforce edges and contact points to prevent movement
Perform final inspection to confirm the opening is safely secured and stabilized
Clean the work area

Tech reported that the exterior metal wall panels and warehouse overhead door have sustained impact damage and require replacement to restore the building envelope and secure building access.

Remove and dispose of all temporary wood framing and board-up materials
Remove and dispose of the damaged overhead door, tracks, springs, hardware, and operating components
Remove and dispose of the damaged exterior metal wall panels, trim, flashing, and fasteners
Repair and reinforce damaged framing members to provide proper support for the new installation
Prepare the wall opening and overhead door opening for installation
Supply and install new pre-finished metal wall panels matching the existing profile, gauge, and finish
Supply and install new trim, closures, flashing, fasteners, and weatherproof sealants
Supply and install a new 10x10 commercial sectional overhead door sized to fit the existing opening
Supply and install new vertical and horizontal tracks, rollers, hinges, torsion spring assembly, lift cables, bearing plates, bottom seal, perimeter weather seals, and all associated operating hardware

Verify proper door alignment, balance, track clearance, and spring tension
Adjust all hardware and operating components to ensure safe and reliable operation
Test the overhead door through multiple open and close cycles

Perform final testing

Tech reported that he standing ice cream freezer is not maintaining the required operating temperature due to a contaminated refrigeration system, a restricted filter drier, a dirty condenser coil, and an improperly adjusted thermostatic expansion valve (TXV)

Required is to
Perform full inspection of the work area
Shut down the freezer and isolate electrical power
Recover refrigerant from the refrigeration system
Remove and dispose of existing filter drier
Flush the refrigeration circuit using RX-11 flushing solvent
Install acid scavenger to remove moisture and acid contamination from the refrigeration system
Supply and install new OEM filter drier (Zero Zone P/N 69-0842-2Y)
Clean condenser coil
Evacuate the refrigeration system to remove air and moisture
Recharge the system with the designated type and quantity of refrigerant
Adjust and calibrate the thermostatic expansion valve (TXV) to achieve the proper evaporator temperature and refrigerant flow
Verify superheat, suction pressure, discharge pressure and compressor operation
Test freezer operation and confirm product holding temperature suitable for ice cream storage
Final testing and commissioning
Clean the work area

Tech Reported that Grill #4 was operating with an improper air-to-fuel mixture caused by debris accumulation within the burner assembly. The thermostat calibration is also out of adjustment, affecting temperature accuracy

Perform full inspection of the work area
Inspect and troubleshoot Grill #4
Clean burner assembly, air shutter and burner venturi to remove grease, dust and debris
Adjust air shutter to restore proper air-to-fuel mixture
Recalibrate thermostat to manufacturer specifications
Verify burner flame characteristics and temperature accuracy
Test grill operation through multiple heating cycles
Confirm thermostat is maintaining the correct set temperature
Final testing and commissioning
Clean the work area

2.5 hours labor Tech $250.00

Total Incurred $250.00

Work has to be performed before/after hours.

Shut off gas supply and isolate the grill
Disassemble grill burner and control assemblies
Remove and dispose of failed thermostat

Verify burner ignition, flame pattern and combustion performance
Test grill through multiple heating cycles
Verify proper temperature regulation and overall operation
Final testing and commissioning
Clean the work area

Tech Reported that the units is not cooling properly, and a temporary water cooled unit needs to be sat up in the kitchen

Note to Customer:
Unit Specs
Manufacturer: Lennox
Model: LGH120H4BH3Y
Serial Number: 5615C06447
Cooling Capacity: 118,000 BTU (10 Ton Nominal)
Refrigerant: R-410A

During inspection, it was noted that a UV dye leak detection product had previously been introduced into the refrigeration system. Additionally, leak sealant was found to be present within the refrigerant circuit. The use of leak sealants is not approved by the equipment manufacturer and may contribute to contamination of the refrigerant, oil, and system components.

Due to the presence of dye and sealant contamination, a complete refrigerant recovery, system flush, and filter drier replacement are recommended prior to further repairs. Following system cleanup, a nitrogen pressure test and comprehensive leak search should be performed to identify the source of refrigerant loss. Once any leaks are repaired, the system can be evacuated and recharged with new refrigerant in accordance with manufacturer specifications.

Please note that the full extent of the damage cannot be determined at this time. Additional issues may be discovered during the flushing, leak testing, and repair process due to contamination within the refrigeration circuit. Any additional repairs identified will be documented and quoted separately if required.

Required is to:
Perform full inspection of the work area
Supply and install a 1.5 Ton water cooled HVAC unit
Supply and install a 120 V 15/20 amp 50' Extension Cord
Supply and install a 5 channel cable ramp
Perform final testing 
Clean the work area

Perform full inspection of the work area and system components
Diagnose and troubleshoot system operation and identify refrigerant leak source
Shut down unit and disconnect electrical power
Recover refrigerant from system and dispose/handle per EPA regulations
Repair identified refrigerant leak
Replace liquid line filter drier
Perform nitrogen pressure test to verify system integrity
Evacuate system to 500 microns and verify vacuum hold

Reconnect and secure all electrical components
Restore power and start system
Verify proper operation including superheat, subcooling, airflow, and pressures
Perform full coil cleaning and replace air filters

Clean work area and remove all debris

Tech reported that Fan 3 requires replacement, Fan 4 requires a new belt and cleaning, and Fans 1 and 2 should be cleaned and maintained to prevent future failures

Required is to:
Perform full inspection of kitchen exhaust system including hoods, filters, ductwork, rooftop exhaust fans, and associated components
Remove grease buildup from fan housings, fan wheels, blades, curb assemblies, and associated components
Clean Fan 1 and Fan 2 assemblies, including housings, blades, motors, and accessible duct connections
Clean Fan 3 and Fan 4 housing, blades, and associated components
Disconnect and isolate electrical power to exhaust fan equipment
Remove and dispose of failed Fan 3 and Fan 4 exhaust fan motor assembly
Supply and install new exhaust fan motor assembly for Fan 3 and 4
Supply and install new drive belts for Fan 3 and Fan 4
Align and adjust pulleys, sheaves, and belt drives to manufacturer specifications
Lubricate bearings and moving components
Reassemble all fan components and verify proper installation
Restore electrical service and perform operational testing of all exhaust fans
Verify proper airflow and exhaust performance throughout the kitchen exhaust system
Inspect system for excessive grease accumulation and fire hazards
Remove all debris generated during cleaning and repair operations
Perform final testing and commissioning
Clean the work area

The scope of work does not include cleaning the kitchen hoods or ductwork. It is limited to removing the grease buildup from the exhaust fan housings to facilitate the replacement of the two failed exhaust fan motors and the repairs to the remaining two exhaust fans.

Defrost evaporator coil and remove ice accumulation from coil surfaces and drain area
Inspect refrigerant lines and fittings for signs of leakage and oil residue
Perform refrigerant pressure check and verify low charge condition
Conduct leak inspection on accessible refrigerant piping and connections
Perform deep vacuum on system to remove moisture and non condensable
Recharge system with 4 lbs. of refrigerant to manufacturer specifications
Restore power to unit and initiate startup
Monitor evaporator operation and verify proper frost pattern and airflow
Verify refrigerant pressures and temperature performance
Perform final testing and commissioning 
Clean the work area

Perform final testing and commissioning

Tech reported that approximately 100-125 square feet of ceiling in the men’s and women’s restrooms has sustained water damage

Required is to:
Perform full inspection of the work area
Shut off water for the women's restroom 
Cut damaged section of pipe in the women's restroom 
Remove and dispose of compromised piping materials
Prepare pipe ends for new connection
Supply and install new pipe section compatible with existing plumbing
Install fittings and couplings to reconnect the line
Secure all joints and ensure proper alignment
Supply, cut and install new woods studs underneath the pipe
Restore water supply and pressurize system
Cut and remove compromised ceiling panels and framing and fixtures
Remove and dispose of collapsed ceiling drywall panels and water damaged sections in both restrooms
Allow affected areas to dry and treat surfaces to prevent further deterioration
Replace damaged framing and support components to restore structural stability
Supply and install new ceiling drywall panels in both restrooms to match existing layout and configuration
Tape and finish all seams and joints to achieve smooth surface transition
Sand repaired areas to create uniform finish
Apply primer to repaired ceiling sections
Apply paint to match existing restroom ceiling finish
Reinstall ceiling components and fixtures
Perform final testing 
Clean the work area

custom_fields.value:
Tech Reported that the patio mister pump has damaged high-pressure brass adapters, compression fittings, and stainless steel high-pressure washers that need replacement

Required is to
Perform full assessment of patio mister pump and high-pressure misting connections
Shut down and isolate pump system
Relieve pressure from misting line before repair
Remove and dispose of damaged high-pressure brass adapters, damaged high-pressure compression fittings, and worn stainless steel high-pressure washers
Supply and install new high-pressure brass adapters, high-pressure compression fittings, and stainless steel high-pressure washers
Reconnect misting line connections to pump assembly
Secure all fittings and verify proper alignment
Restore water supply and power to patio mister pump
Pressure test system and inspect all repaired connections for leaks
Clean work area

Incurred:
Trip  $75.00
1 hour labor Troubleshooting  $129.00
2.5 hours labor Tech 1  $322.50
High-Pressure Brass Adapters  $165.94

Total Incurred $692.44

Additional Repair:

We troubleshot the patio misting system and replaced the failed high-pressure brass adapters, compression fittings, and stainless-steel washers. After completing the repairs, the system was retested and continued to operate improperly. Further troubleshooting determined the failure extends beyond the external connection components and is originating within the misting pump assembly.
Due to the condition of the existing unit and the extent of the failure, additional repairs cannot be recommended as a reliable or cost-effective solution. Replacement of the patio mister pump system is recommended to restore proper operation and reliability.

Required is to: Replacing the patio mister unit with a matching misting pump system
Shut down and isolate electrical power and water supply to the existing patio mister unit.
Remove and dispose of the existing patio mister pump assembly and any damaged or worn connection components.
Supply and install a new FG-700 patio mister pump system, including all required adapters, fittings, washers, electrical connection materials, and accessories required for installation.
Reconnect the existing water supply, high-pressure misting lines, and electrical connections to the new pump assembly.
Prime, start up, and test the new patio mister system, verifying proper pump operation, operating pressure, water flow, mist output, leak-free connections, and system controls.
Perform final testing, commissioning, and cleanup of the work area.

Specs:
QTY 1 - OEM FG-700, 7.0 L/min, 1.2 kW motor, 3 piston pump, 70 bar pressure.

Labor:
6.5 hours labor Tech 1 OT  $1257.75
6.5 hours labor Tech 2 OT  $1257.75

Total Labor $2515.50

Recharge system with 3 lbs. of refrigerant to manufacturer specifications
